### Concepts

| Question | Answer in brief |
|---|---|
| What is the virtual DOM? | An in-memory tree of elements that React compares to find minimal DOM changes |
| Why are keys needed? | To match list items across renders; index keys break on reorder |
| Controlled or uncontrolled? | State owns the value, or the DOM does |
| Why are hooks only at the top level? | React tracks them by call order |
| What are the phases? | Render (pure), then commit (DOM changes), then effects |
| What triggers a render? | Its state, its parent, or a context |
| `useEffect` or `useLayoutEffect`? | After paint, or before paint for measuring |
| What's prop drilling? | Passing props through layers; use composition or context |
| What's an error boundary? | A component that catches render errors below it |
| Why not mutate state? | React compares references |
| What is batching? | Several updates in one render |
| What are portals? | Rendering to another DOM place, as for modals |
| Why use `lazy` and `Suspense`? | Load code when needed, with a fallback |
| What's the React Compiler? | A build tool that memoises automatically |

### Predict the behaviour

blocks.title: How many times does it log, and what does the screen show?

blocks.text: After one click, the screen shows 2. The first two calls each set 1, and the updater adds 1 to the latest value. Batching means one extra render (ignoring Strict Mode).

blocks.title: Find the bug

blocks.text:
This one has several problems: no dependency array means that it fetches after every render, and `setResults` causes another render, so **an infinite loop**. It also has no race handling, no `res.ok` check, no URL encoding, and no debounce.

### Class components

Older code uses them, so recognise `componentDidMount`, `componentDidUpdate` and `componentWillUnmount`, which map roughly to `useEffect`, plus `this.state` and `this.setState`.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Be ready to explain render and commit
- Spot infinite effect loops
- Keys and references come up often
- Recognise class components

### Worked problem: autocomplete

**Requirements:** type to search users from an API, with suggestions, keyboard navigation, and no stale results.

blocks.title: An autocomplete search

blocks.text:
Things worth saying aloud: debounce saves requests, abort handles races, `encodeURIComponent` prevents broken URLs, and in real work you'd add a full ARIA combobox pattern, or use a tested library.

### More problems to practise

| Problem | Key skills |
|---|---|
| Todo list with filters and persistence | State, derived data, localStorage |
| Pagination and sortable data table | URL state, derived data |
| Infinite scroll feed | `IntersectionObserver`, cursor pages |
| Modal with focus handling | Portals, accessibility |
| Star rating | Controlled component, hover state |
| Multi-step form | Reducer, validation |
| Tic-tac-toe | State, derived winner, immutable updates |
| Tabs and accordion | Composition, keyboard support |
| Countdown or stopwatch | Effects, cleanup, stale closures |
| Nested comments | Recursion |
| Kanban board | Lists, drag and drop |
| Shopping cart | Reducer, totals, money handling |

### Frontend system design

For experienced roles, you may be asked to design a news feed, a chat app or a shared document. Cover these areas:

| Area | Questions |
|---|---|
| Requirements | Users, devices, scale, offline? |
| Architecture | CSR or SSR, routing, code splitting |
| Data | API shape, caching, pagination, real time |
| State | Server, URL, local |
| Performance | Bundles, images, virtualised lists |
| Accessibility and i18n | Keyboard, screen readers, languages |
| Reliability | Errors, retries, monitoring |
| Security | XSS, CSRF, tokens |

### For full stack candidates

Interviewers often connect the two halves. Be ready to walk through what happens when a user clicks Save, from `onClick` through fetch, CORS, the load balancer, the Spring Security filter chain, the controller, the transaction and the response, to the cache update and re-render. Few candidates can tell the whole story, and it's a strong way to show that you really are full stack.

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant R as React
  participant Q as Query cache
  participant S as Spring Boot
  participant D as Database
  U->>R: Click Save
  R->>S: POST /api/orders with token
  S->>S: Security filter, validation
  S->>D: Transaction: insert order and outbox
  D-->>S: Committed
  S-->>R: 201 with order JSON
  R->>Q: Invalidate orders
  Q->>S: GET /api/orders
  S-->>Q: Latest list
  Q-->>R: New data
  R-->>U: Re-render with the new order
blocks.title: The full stack journey of a click

blocks.text:
### What to build for a portfolio

One polished project beats several half-finished ones. Connect a React and TypeScript frontend to your Spring Boot API, with authentication, TanStack Query, handled states, responsive design and tests, and deploy it. A live link, plus a README with a screenshot and your decisions, helps a lot for a fresher.

**"Why React rather than plain JavaScript?"** Describing UI as a function of state avoids manual DOM syncing, and components make large screens manageable. The trade-offs are bundle size, tooling and a build step, so very simple pages may not need it.
blocks.title: Interview answer
Key points
blocks.text:
- Clarify, plan, then build
- Handle states, even under time pressure
- Say your trade-offs aloud
- Tell the full journey of a click

sections.title: Worked machine coding: Todo and data table

blocks.text:
### Problem 1: Todo with filters and persistence

**Requirements:** add, toggle and delete; filter by all, active and done; survive a refresh.

blocks.title: A complete solution

blocks.text:
**What earns marks:** a pure reducer, lazy initial load, derived `visible` and `remaining`, no stored duplicates, stable IDs as keys, trimmed input, an empty state and accessible controls.

### Problem 2: a sortable, paginated table

blocks.title: Everything is derived from three values

blocks.text:
**Points to mention:** copy before sorting, since `sort` mutates. Use `localeCompare` for text. Clamp the page if data shrinks. Reset the page on sort. Add `aria-sort`. In production, large tables sort and paginate on the server, and state lives in the URL.

### What interviewers notice

| Good signs | Bad signs |
|---|---|
| Asks questions first | Starts typing at once |
| Runs the code often | Writes everything, and then tests |
| Handles empty and error states | Only the happy path |
| Clear names and small components | One 300-line component |
| Says trade-offs aloud | Works in silence |
| Admits what they'd do with more time | Pretends it's complete |

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Reducers keep the logic testable
- Derive filtered lists and counts
- Copy before sorting
- Clamp the page when data shrinks

sections.title: Frontend system design: a news feed

blocks.text:
Experienced candidates may be asked to design a frontend architecture. A strong answer follows a structure. Even as a fresher, this helps you talk about your own project.

### 1. Clarify requirements

**Functional:** infinite feed, like and comment, new post notifications, images and video. **Non-functional:** works on slow phones, accessible, fast first load, handles lost connections.

### 2. Architecture

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A[App shell: server-rendered or static] --> B[Feed route]
  B --> C[Query cache: posts by cursor]
  C --> D[API: GET /feed?cursor]
  B --> E[Virtualised list]
  E --> F[PostCard]
  F --> G[Optimistic like mutation]
  H[SSE or WebSocket] --> I[New posts banner]
  I --> C
blocks.title: A news feed's architecture

blocks.text: ### 3. Data model and API

blocks.title: Client types and API

blocks.text:
Use **cursor pagination**: offset pages shift when new posts arrive, which causes duplicates and gaps.

### 4. Hard parts

| Problem | Approach |
|---|---|
| Very long list | Virtualise; keep a limited number of pages in memory |
| New posts while reading | Show "3 new posts" and don't jump the scroll position |
| Images | Reserve space with `aspect-ratio`, lazy load, sized variants |
| Autoplaying video | Play only when in view, using `IntersectionObserver` |
| Like button | Optimistic update, with rollback |
| Going offline | Show cached feed and a banner; queue likes, or disable them |
| Duplicate posts across pages | De-duplicate by ID |
| Returning to the feed | Restore scroll, using the cached pages |

### 5. Performance plan

Split routes. Render a static shell. Send critical CSS first. Serve images through a CDN, with `srcset`. Prefetch the next page as the user nears the end. Keep the main thread free for smooth scrolling.

### 6. Accessibility

Use `article` per post, a feed role, keyboard shortcuts for next and previous, labelled buttons, and an announcement for new posts. Virtualisation needs care, as off-screen items don't exist for screen readers, so provide proper set sizes and positions.

### 7. Reliability and security

Retry reads with backoff, and show inline errors per post rather than breaking the whole page. Sanitise any user-provided HTML, and render user text as text. Track errors and Web Vitals by release.

### Practice questions

| Design | Focus on |
|---|---|
| Autocomplete | Debounce, cache, races, keyboard and ARIA |
| Chat app | WebSocket, ordering, offline queue, optimistic send |
| Image carousel | Lazy loading, gestures, accessibility |
| Data dashboard | Virtual tables, charts, polling, saved filters |
| Google Docs-like editor | Conflict handling, presence (a stretch) |

**"Design X."** Spend the first minutes on requirements, then components and data flow, then API and state, and go deep on the hardest part. Finish with performance, accessibility, failure handling and what you would measure.
blocks.title: Interview answer
Key points
blocks.text:
- Clarify first
- Use cursor pagination for feeds
- Don't jump scroll on new posts
- Cover performance, accessibility and failure
#### Output questions, worked

items.question: What does [1, 2, 3].map(parseInt) return, and why?
items.answer: [1, NaN, NaN]. map passes the index as parseInt's radix.

items.question: Why does the code before an await run immediately?
items.answer: An async function runs synchronously until its first await.

items.question: How do debounce and throttle differ?
items.answer: Debounce waits until calls stop. Throttle runs at most once per interval.

blocks.text: #### React questions

items.question: Why does an effect with no dependency array that sets state cause a loop?
items.answer: Each state change renders, and the effect runs after every render, setting state again.

items.question: What's the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect?
items.answer: useEffect usually runs after paint. useLayoutEffect runs before paint, for DOM measurement, and can block painting.

blocks.text: #### Machine coding rounds

items.question: In a machine coding round, what do you build first?
items.answer: The simplest working happy path, then loading, empty and error states, then polish.

items.question: Why does the autocomplete hook both clear a timer and abort?
items.answer: Clearing stops a request that hasn't started, and aborting cancels one in progress, so stale results can't overwrite new ones.

items.question: How do you show you're truly full stack in an interview?
items.answer: Trace one action from the click, through the network and server to the database, and back to the re-render.

blocks.text: #### More output questions

items.question: What does [1, 2].map((n) => { n * 2 }) give?
items.answer: [undefined, undefined], as a block body has no implicit return.

items.question: Why does obj[{ id: 2 }] overwrite obj[{ id: 1 }]?
items.answer: Both keys become the string '[object Object]'. A Map keeps them apart.

items.question: Why does m.get({ id: 1 }) return undefined after setting that key?
items.answer: It's a different object. Map compares keys by reference.

blocks.text: #### Worked machine coding: Todo and data table

items.question: Why pass a loader function as useReducer's third argument?
items.answer: It runs only once at start, rather than reading storage on every render.

items.question: What goes wrong if you call rows.sort() directly on a prop?
items.answer: It mutates the parent's array, breaking React's assumptions, and can cause bugs elsewhere.

items.question: Why clamp the page number?
items.answer: If data shrinks, a stale page may no longer exist, and would show nothing.

blocks.text: #### Frontend system design: a news feed

items.question: Why use a cursor rather than an offset for a feed?
items.answer: New posts shift offsets, causing duplicates and gaps. A cursor stays stable.

items.question: How do you show new posts without disturbing the reader?
items.answer: Show a banner, and add them when clicked, preserving scroll position.

items.question: How do you avoid layout shifts in an image feed?
items.answer: Reserve space with known dimensions or `aspect-ratio`.
